messages:
eli: Heads-up — seeing a perf regression after the kernel-picker 2.3 rollout. Replay harness with mostly-hot prefix traffic shows throughput down ~8-12% vs baseline. Need a quick smoke/bisect. :thinking:

maya: Ugh. Which replay trace and model config? Is this isolated to prefetched KV workloads?

eli: Replay trace is kv-prefill-aug2026 (mix: 60% short prefixes, 30% long, 10% cold). Model: gptx-13b-quant on A100s. Repro command I ran locally: ```bash
./replay_harness --trace=kv-prefill-aug2026 --duration=15m --seed=2026 --concurrency=48 --kernel-strategy=auto
```

tj: Can you try forcing legacy selector? Trying to narrow kernel-picker delta vs kernel implementation. Env var: `RR_KERNEL_STRATEGY=legacy` or `=aggressive`.

eli: Yep, forced legacy and perf went back to baseline (~+10% throughput). So something in the selector heuristics (maybe sequence-length bucketing) is picking smaller attention kernels more often.

ciara: I profiled a run with `perf` + flamegraph. Short snippet from the hotspot summary: ```
# samples  %time  symbol
1240  15.3  attention_kernel_v2
980   12.1  kv_cache_lookup
620    7.6  batch_coalesce
540    6.7  kernel_dispatcher::choose
```
So dispatcher/choose is nontrivial. Looks like increased overhead on the selector path when batch size is high.

maya: Do we have a microbenchmark that isolates selector latency vs kernel execution? Might be small overhead but multiplied by many requests.

eli: I added a tiny harness: single-request path that calls selector 100k times and measures median. Result: selector median went from 40us -> 110us after 2.3 in the high-entropy sequence distribution. Attaches the gist: https://internal/gists/sel-bench-1951234567

kv-replay-bot: Job finished: replay/1951234567 — logs: https://internal/logs/replay/1951234567 — throughput_drop=10.8% — traces=3/3 failing threshold

tj: That matches. Hypothesis: new heuristic computes a per-prefix kernel plan that does extra allocation/formatting when prefix lengths vary a lot. Two quick fixes: cache the plan key (cheap) or avoid computing plan for small batches.

ciara: I pushed a quick patch that memoizes plan selection keyed by (model, seqlen_bucket, quant_mode). Patch: ```diff
+ static absl::flat_hash_map<Key, Plan> plan_cache;
+ if (auto it = plan_cache.find(k); it != plan_cache.end()) return it->second;
```
Smoke on my local shows selector median back to ~45us and replay throughput within 2% of baseline.

maya: Nice. Can you open a PR with perf tests? We should add an apples-to-apples replay harness that runs old selector vs new with identical seeds and compare hitrates + per-request selector time.

eli: On it — will include: 1) replay trace, 2) synth-mix with controlled prefix hotness, 3) selector microbench, 4) KV hitrate/time series. Also adding CI perf job that runs nightly on a small cluster.

tj: Also validate eviction behavior under concurrency — the new selector might change access patterns causing different eviction churn. Add a KV warmup monitor for prefix hit rate over time and eviction counts.

ciara: Added sample prometheus queries: `rate(kv_evictions_total[5m])` and `kv_prefix_hitrate{trace="kv-prefill-aug2026"}`. In the failing runs evictions spike ~3x during the first 2 minutes.

eli: Good call. If eviction churn is higher we need to consider lock contention too. I saw `kv_cache_lookup` acquire time increase by ~30% in `perf` flame.

kv-replay-bot: Benchmark snapshot uploaded: s3://perf-artifacts/replay/1951234567/snapshot.tar.gz

maya: Plan: eli + ciara submit PR with memoize + perf tests, tj runs a canary on staging dedicated pool with both strategies, and we roll back if replay nightly shows >5% regression.

eli: I'll draft the PR and include the microbench results and the minimal repro script. cc @tj for canary schedule. :thumbsup:

tj: Sounds good. If patch holds, we still want an upstream improvement to reduce selector CPU for future kernel variants (maybe precompile plan tables during model load).

ciara: Agreed. I'll prototype precompile in the model load path next week.

eli: Thanks all — I'll post PR link here when ready.
